title: Chronic Kidney Disease
sourceTitle: Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management
locator: Recommendations 1.1.1 to 1.1.14, Table 1 and recommendations 1.5.5 to 1.5.7
scope: Adults with suspected or established chronic kidney disease; this limited extraction covers eGFR, urine albumin:creatinine ratio, classification, progression and specialist-referral triggers.
gaps: NICE NG203 is a UK guideline and requires reconciliation with current Saudi nephrology pathways, local laboratory reporting and referral capacity. The source names ACE inhibitors and angiotensin-receptor blockers but this extraction does not support a complete medicine choice, dose, route, frequency, duration or contraindication set. Existing inherited treatment text and references are not newly verified.

investigations.test: Serum creatinine with estimated glomerular filtration rate
investigations.question: Is reduced kidney function present and persistent?
investigations.finding: Use creatinine-based eGFR in adults; a new eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² should be repeated to confirm the result.
investigations.rationale: NICE uses eGFR to detect and classify reduced kidney function while recognising biological and analytical variability.
investigations.timeframe: Repeat a new eGFR below 60 within 2 weeks; use serial results to establish chronicity and progression

investigations.question: Is clinically important albuminuria present?
investigations.finding: An ACR of 3 to 70 mg/mmol should be confirmed on a subsequent early-morning sample; an initial ACR of 70 mg/mmol or more does not require repeat confirmation.
investigations.rationale: Albuminuria is required with GFR category to classify CKD and informs referral and management.
investigations.timeframe: At initial CKD assessment; confirm 3 to 70 mg/mmol using an early-morning sample

investigations.question: Does the person meet a risk-based specialist-referral threshold?
investigations.finding: A 5-year risk of needing renal replacement therapy above 5% is one NICE referral criterion.
investigations.rationale: Risk prediction supplements eGFR, ACR, haematuria, blood pressure and rate-of-decline criteria.
investigations.timeframe: Use in adults with CKD stages G3a to G5 when making referral decisions

actions.instruction: Classify CKD using both GFR and ACR categories and document the cause when known.

Refer for specialist assessment when a NICE criterion is met, including 5-year kidney-failure risk above 5%, ACR 70 mg/mmol or more, ACR above 30 mg/mmol with haematuria, defined sustained eGFR decline, or resistant hypertension.

title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
sourceTitle: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in over 16s: diagnosis and management
edition: NG115, published 5 December 2018; last updated 26 July 2019
scope: People aged over 16 with suspected or diagnosed COPD; this limited extraction covers diagnostic spirometry, selected baseline tests, dyspnoea assessment and routine review.
gaps: This older UK source requires reconciliation with current GOLD, Saudi respiratory guidance and local spirometry standards before approval. Interpretation should account for current GLI reference equations and population limitations. The source contains treatment recommendations, but this limited extraction does not verify a complete medicine regimen, inhaler choice, dose, device, duration or contraindication set. Existing inherited sections are not newly verified.

investigations.question: Is persistent airflow obstruction present in a person with compatible symptoms and risk factors?
investigations.finding: Post-bronchodilator spirometry is used to confirm COPD; interpret the result with the clinical picture and alternative diagnoses.
investigations.rationale: NICE requires objective demonstration of airflow obstruction rather than diagnosis from symptoms alone.
investigations.timeframe: At diagnostic assessment

investigations.test: Chest radiograph and full blood count
investigations.question: Are an alternative diagnosis, comorbidity, anaemia or polycythaemia contributing?
investigations.finding: A chest radiograph and full blood count are included in initial diagnostic investigations.
investigations.rationale: These tests help identify alternative or associated disease that changes management.
investigations.timeframe: At initial diagnostic work-up

investigations.question: Is inherited alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency plausible?
investigations.finding: Testing is considered for early-onset disease, minimal smoking history or family history.
investigations.rationale: A positive diagnosis affects counselling and specialist management.
investigations.timeframe: When clinical features suggest inherited deficiency

actions.instruction: Record breathlessness using the MRC dyspnoea scale and assess exacerbation history, smoking status, oxygen saturation, BMI and comorbidities.
Review people with COPD at least annually, with more frequent review when clinically indicated.

title: Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment Planning
edition: NG151, published 29 January 2020; recommendations page includes updates through 2025
locator: Recommendations on staging, molecular testing, treatment planning and follow-up after curative treatment
scope: Adults with confirmed or suspected colorectal cancer; this limited extraction covers staging, selected tumour biomarkers, multidisciplinary treatment planning and surveillance after curative treatment.
gaps: The current NICE page links to technology appraisals that may change medicine eligibility. This extraction does not reproduce systemic anticancer regimens, doses, contraindications, operative detail or radiotherapy schedules. All treatment must be reconciled with current Saudi oncology protocols, tumour site and stage, pathology, molecular results, performance status and multidisciplinary review. Existing inherited sections and references are not newly verified.

investigations.question: Is colorectal malignancy confirmed and what is the local and distant extent?
investigations.finding: Tissue diagnosis and stage-appropriate imaging establish tumour type, local extent and metastatic disease for treatment planning.
investigations.rationale: Treatment selection depends on confirmed pathology, tumour site and stage.
investigations.timeframe: Before definitive treatment planning

investigations.test: RAS and BRAF V600E mutation testing
investigations.question: Does metastatic disease have a molecular profile that changes systemic-treatment options?
investigations.finding: RAS and BRAF V600E status should be available for people with metastatic colorectal cancer who may be candidates for systemic treatment.
investigations.rationale: These biomarkers affect eligibility for targeted treatment and prognosis.
investigations.timeframe: Before selecting systemic treatment for metastatic disease

investigations.question: Does the tumour have deficient mismatch repair or high microsatellite instability?
investigations.finding: MMR or MSI status informs hereditary assessment and treatment options in relevant disease settings.
investigations.rationale: Molecular classification can change counselling and systemic-treatment decisions.
investigations.timeframe: During pathological and molecular work-up

actions.instruction: Review confirmed disease in a colorectal multidisciplinary team using tumour site, stage, pathology, molecular findings, comorbidity, performance status and patient preferences.
After curative treatment, use surveillance that includes CEA testing and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis during the first 3 years, individualised to recurrence risk and treatment suitability.
actions.timeframe: During the first 3 years after curative treatment

title: Colorectal Cancer Screening
sourceTitle: USPSTF Colorectal Cancer: Screening Final Recommendation Statement
locator: Recommendation Summary and Practice Considerations: Patient Population Under Consideration and Screening Tests
scope: Asymptomatic average-risk adults aged 45 years or older without prior colorectal cancer, adenomatous polyps, inflammatory bowel disease or a known high-risk genetic syndrome.
gaps: This is a United States recommendation and must be reconciled with the current Saudi national screening programme, local test availability, eligibility and colonoscopy capacity. It does not apply to symptomatic or high-risk people. Harms, bowel preparation, sedation, test-quality requirements and post-polypectomy surveillance are not fully specified in this extraction.

investigations.question: Which non-invasive screening interval is suitable for an average-risk adult?
investigations.finding: Supported strategies include annual FIT and stool DNA-FIT every 1 to 3 years.
investigations.rationale: Regular stool testing can reduce colorectal-cancer mortality when positive results receive colonoscopy.
investigations.timeframe: FIT every year or stool DNA-FIT every 1 to 3 years

investigations.question: Which structural examination and interval is suitable?
investigations.finding: Supported strategies include CT colonography every 5 years, flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years, colonoscopy every 10 years, or flexible sigmoidoscopy every 10 years combined with annual FIT.
investigations.rationale: These strategies balance test burden, interval and ability to detect colorectal lesions.
investigations.timeframe: At the interval specified for the selected strategy

investigations.test: Diagnostic colonoscopy after an abnormal screening test
investigations.question: Has a non-colonoscopy screening test returned an abnormal result?
investigations.finding: The screening benefit is not achieved unless an abnormal stool, CT-colonography or sigmoidoscopy result receives colonoscopic evaluation.
investigations.rationale: Colonoscopy completes diagnostic evaluation and permits biopsy or polyp management.
investigations.timeframe: Promptly after an abnormal screening result

actions.instruction: Offer screening to average-risk adults aged 45 to 75 using an evidence-supported strategy selected through shared decision-making.
Selectively offer screening at ages 76 to 85 according to overall health, prior screening history and preferences; do not continue routine screening after age 85.

title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
locator: Recommendations on CRB65 and CURB65, hospital chest radiography, microbiological testing, Table 1 adult antibiotics and review of treatment duration
scope: Adults with community-acquired pneumonia; this limited extraction covers severity assessment, hospital diagnosis, selected microbiology and one first-choice low-severity oral antibiotic regimen.
gaps: This UK guideline requires reconciliation with Saudi antimicrobial policy, local resistance, allergy history, renal and hepatic function, pregnancy, QT risk, interactions and microbiology. The exact contraindication set is not provided on the retrieved recommendation page and must be checked against the current product information and local formulary before use. Moderate and high-severity regimens, aspiration, immunocompromise and recent healthcare exposure are outside this limited extraction. Existing inherited sections are not newly verified.

investigations.question: What is the risk of mortality and appropriate place of care?
investigations.finding: Use CRB65 in primary care and CURB65 in hospital alongside clinical judgement.
investigations.rationale: Severity scoring supports escalation and site-of-care decisions but does not replace clinical assessment.
investigations.timeframe: At first assessment

investigations.question: Is pneumonia confirmed in a person admitted to hospital?
investigations.finding: Hospital services should establish the diagnosis, including chest radiography, promptly after presentation.
investigations.rationale: Rapid confirmation supports timely treatment and review of alternative diagnoses.
investigations.timeframe: Within 4 hours of hospital presentation

investigations.question: Is pathogen testing likely to change treatment?
investigations.finding: Routine microbiological testing is not recommended for low-severity community-acquired pneumonia; consider testing when severity or clinical context warrants it.
investigations.rationale: Testing is targeted to cases where results can influence antibiotic choice or public-health action.
investigations.timeframe: Before or early in antibiotic treatment when indicated

actions.instruction: Start antibiotics promptly after diagnosis and reassess if symptoms worsen rapidly, fail to improve as expected or suggest sepsis.
actions.timeframe: As soon as pneumonia is diagnosed

actions.instruction: Stop antibiotic treatment after 5 days unless microbiological results or clinical instability indicate a longer course.

medicines.indication: First-choice oral treatment for low-severity community-acquired pneumonia in adults
medicines.group: Adults with low-severity community-acquired pneumonia when penicillin is suitable
adjustments: Use an alternative regimen when penicillin allergy or another contraindication is present.
Reconcile renal adjustment, pregnancy, interactions and local resistance with the current local formulary.
monitoring: Review clinical response and signs of instability.
Review microbiology when obtained and narrow or change therapy as indicated.

title: Conservative Kidney Care Planning
sourceTitle: Renal replacement therapy and conservative management
locator: Recommendations on indications for renal replacement therapy or conservative management, information and decision-making, and dietary assessment
scope: Adults approaching kidney failure who are considering renal replacement therapy or comprehensive conservative kidney care; this limited extraction covers early assessment, shared decisions and symptom-focused planning.
gaps: This older UK guideline requires reconciliation with current Saudi nephrology, transplantation, dialysis and palliative-care pathways. Prognostic tools, emergency dialysis indications, medicine prescribing, exact symptom-control doses and contraindications are not verified in this extraction. Existing inherited sections and references are not newly verified.

investigations.question: Is kidney failure likely within the planning horizon and what options fit the person's clinical state and goals?
investigations.finding: Assessment integrates kidney trajectory, symptoms, comorbidity, expected quality of life, life expectancy and personal preferences.
investigations.rationale: The choice between renal replacement therapy and conservative management should be made before a crisis and revisited as circumstances change.
investigations.timeframe: Begin at least 1 year before renal replacement therapy is likely to be needed

investigations.question: Which physical, psychological, social or spiritual symptoms require treatment or support?
investigations.finding: Ongoing review identifies symptom burden and changing supportive-care needs.
investigations.rationale: Conservative kidney care is an active, comprehensive pathway centred on quality of life.
investigations.timeframe: Throughout conservative management and whenever condition or goals change

investigations.question: Can nutrition advice improve symptoms and safety without causing malnutrition?
investigations.finding: A specialist renal dietitian assesses dietary needs and individualises advice.
investigations.rationale: Dietary restrictions and symptom-focused changes require assessment of nutritional risk and preferences.
investigations.timeframe: During planning and review

actions.instruction: Offer balanced information and a choice between appropriate renal replacement options and conservative management, using joint decision-making.
actions.timeframe: During advance planning and at major clinical changes

actions.instruction: Document goals, preferred place of care, escalation decisions, symptom plan and how the decision will be reviewed.
actions.timeframe: After shared decision-making and whenever preferences change

title: Deep-Vein Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism
sourceTitle: Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
scope: Adults with suspected or confirmed deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism; this limited extraction covers Wells-based diagnostic pathways, interim anticoagulation safeguards and minimum treatment duration.
gaps: This UK guideline requires reconciliation with current Saudi VTE pathways, local imaging access, pregnancy and cancer protocols, renal and hepatic function, bleeding risk, interactions and product information. Although apixaban and rivaroxaban are named, the retrieved page does not provide a complete dose, route, frequency, switching, duration and contraindication set in this extraction, so no medicine regimen is encoded. Existing inherited sections are not newly verified.

investigations.test: Two-level DVT Wells score with proximal-leg-vein ultrasound and D-dimer pathway
investigations.question: How likely is DVT and which test is required next?
investigations.finding: Use the two-level DVT Wells score; likely DVT proceeds urgently to proximal-leg-vein ultrasound, while D-dimer participates in the pathway according to probability and imaging result.
investigations.rationale: Pretest probability guides safe sequencing of D-dimer, imaging and interim anticoagulation.
investigations.timeframe: At first assessment; obtain definitive testing within the NICE time windows

investigations.test: Two-level PE Wells score with CTPA or D-dimer pathway
investigations.question: How likely is pulmonary embolism and which test is required next?
investigations.finding: Use the two-level PE Wells score; likely PE proceeds to CTPA when suitable, while D-dimer is used for unlikely PE.
investigations.rationale: Structured probability assessment reduces delayed diagnosis and unnecessary imaging.
investigations.timeframe: At first assessment; obtain definitive testing urgently

investigations.test: Baseline full blood count, renal and hepatic function, PT and APTT
investigations.question: Are there baseline abnormalities that affect anticoagulant safety or selection?
investigations.finding: Obtain baseline blood count, kidney and liver function and coagulation tests, but do not delay interim therapeutic anticoagulation while awaiting results.
investigations.rationale: Baseline results guide safe continuation and choice of anticoagulant.
investigations.timeframe: At initiation; review results within 24 hours

actions.instruction: Give interim therapeutic anticoagulation when indicated if definitive diagnostic testing cannot be completed within the recommended timeframe, then review once results are available.
For confirmed proximal DVT or PE, provide anticoagulation for at least 3 months and review ongoing treatment according to provoking factors, bleeding risk and preferences.

title: Delirium and Agitation Near End of Life
sourceTitle: Care of dying adults in the last days of life
locator: Recommendations 1.5.23 to 1.5.28: managing anxiety, delirium and agitation
scope: Adults thought to be in the last days of life who develop anxiety, delirium or agitation; this limited extraction covers reversible causes, non-drug measures and medicine-class trial decisions.
gaps: This is an older UK guideline and must be reconciled with current Saudi palliative-care policy and local specialist protocols. It does not specify an exact drug, dose, route, frequency, duration or complete contraindication set for benzodiazepines or antipsychotics in the retrieved recommendations, so no medicine regimen is encoded. Existing inherited symptom-control text is not newly verified.

investigations.test: Clinical assessment for reversible causes of agitation or delirium
investigations.question: Is distress caused by pain, a full bladder or rectum, metabolic disturbance, medicine effects or another reversible factor?
investigations.finding: Identify and treat reversible causes where this is consistent with the person's goals and last-days-of-life plan.
investigations.rationale: Agitation can be a manifestation of untreated physical distress or delirium rather than a primary psychiatric symptom.
investigations.timeframe: At onset and after each intervention

investigations.test: Assessment of anxiety, delirium and sedation burden
investigations.question: Which syndrome is most likely and has treatment reduced distress without unwanted sedation?
investigations.finding: Repeated bedside assessment guides whether non-drug measures, a medicine-class trial or specialist advice is appropriate.
investigations.rationale: The treatment approach differs for anxiety and delirium and must remain proportionate to comfort goals.
investigations.timeframe: Before treatment and frequently after treatment

actions.instruction: Use non-pharmacological management and address reversible causes before or alongside medicine when appropriate.
Consider a benzodiazepine trial for anxiety or agitation and an antipsychotic trial for delirium or agitation, using the current local palliative protocol and specialist advice.
actions.timeframe: When symptoms remain distressing after assessment

actions.instruction: Seek specialist palliative-care advice if diagnosis is uncertain, treatment does not work or causes unwanted sedation.
actions.timeframe: Promptly when any criterion is present

title: Diabetes Screening in At-Risk Adults
sourceTitle: USPSTF Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Screening Final Recommendation Statement
locator: Recommendation Summary and Practice Considerations: Screening Tests, Screening Intervals and Preventive Interventions
scope: Nonpregnant asymptomatic adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity; this limited extraction covers screening tests, diagnostic thresholds and repeat interval.
gaps: This is a United States preventive recommendation and requires reconciliation with current Saudi diabetes screening policy, ethnicity-specific risk, gestational diabetes history, younger high-risk groups and local laboratory units. It is not a diagnostic pathway for symptomatic hyperglycaemia, pregnancy or acute metabolic decompensation. Medicine prevention is not encoded.

investigations.question: Is fasting glucose in the normal, prediabetes or diabetes range?
investigations.finding: Prediabetes is 100 to 125 mg/dL; diabetes is 126 mg/dL or higher.
investigations.rationale: Fasting plasma glucose is one accepted screening test.
investigations.timeframe: At screening; confirm a diabetes-range result with repeat testing

investigations.question: Does longer-term glycaemia meet a prediabetes or diabetes threshold?
investigations.finding: Prediabetes is 5.7% to 6.4%; diabetes is 6.5% or higher.
investigations.rationale: HbA1c is an accepted screening test and does not require fasting.
investigations.timeframe: At screening; confirm a diabetes-range result with repeat testing

investigations.question: Does the 2-hour glucose meet a prediabetes or diabetes threshold?
investigations.finding: Prediabetes is 140 to 199 mg/dL; diabetes is 200 mg/dL or higher at 2 hours.
investigations.rationale: The oral glucose tolerance test can detect dysglycaemia not apparent on fasting glucose or HbA1c.
investigations.timeframe: At screening when selected; confirm a diabetes-range result

actions.instruction: Screen eligible adults aged 35 to 70 who have overweight or obesity and offer or refer people with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions.
After a normal result, repeating screening every 3 years is a reasonable approach, adjusted for risk and local policy.

title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
sourceTitle: The Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Adults
edition: Joint British Diabetes Societies for Inpatient Care, revised March 2023
locator: PDF pages 9 to 11 and 18 to 25; diagnostic criteria, fluid replacement, fixed-rate intravenous insulin infusion, potassium replacement, monitoring and resolution
scope: Adults with diabetic ketoacidosis; this limited extraction covers diagnostic criteria, initial 0.9% sodium chloride, fixed-rate intravenous soluble human insulin, potassium thresholds, dextrose addition, monitoring and biochemical resolution.
gaps: This March 2023 UK professional guideline predates the 2024 international hyperglycaemic-crises consensus and requires reconciliation with that consensus and the current Saudi emergency, endocrine and critical-care protocol before approval. The source advises cautious fluid replacement in ages 18 to 25, older people, pregnancy, heart failure and renal failure. Exact contraindications are not provided as a complete set; local prescribing and infusion safeguards are mandatory. Paediatric DKA is outside scope. Existing inherited sections are not newly verified.

investigations.test: Capillary glucose, blood ketones and venous blood gas
investigations.question: Are the biochemical criteria for adult DKA present?
investigations.finding: The JBDS criteria are glucose above 11 mmol/L or known diabetes, capillary ketones above 3.0 mmol/L or urine ketones above 2+, and venous pH below 7.3 and/or bicarbonate below 15 mmol/L.
investigations.rationale: All three domains establish hyperglycaemia or diabetes, ketosis and metabolic acidosis.
investigations.timeframe: Immediately at presentation

investigations.question: Are glucose and ketones falling at the expected rate?
investigations.finding: Hourly bedside trends guide insulin and dextrose adjustment.
investigations.rationale: Ketone clearance, rather than glucose alone, is the principal marker of insulin response.
investigations.timeframe: Hourly during active treatment

investigations.test: Venous pH, bicarbonate, potassium and serum electrolytes
investigations.question: Is acidosis resolving and is potassium replacement safe?
investigations.finding: Repeat venous pH, bicarbonate and potassium at 60 minutes, 2 hours and then every 2 hours; check laboratory electrolytes at least every 4 hours.
investigations.rationale: Insulin and fluid therapy can rapidly change potassium and acid-base status.
investigations.timeframe: At 60 minutes, 2 hours, then every 2 hours; laboratory electrolytes every 4 hours

actions.instruction: If systolic blood pressure is below 90 mmHg, give 500 mL 0.9% sodium chloride over 10 to 15 minutes and reassess with senior and critical-care input; once pressure is above 90 mmHg, give 1 litre over 60 minutes. If systolic pressure is at least 90 mmHg initially, give 1 litre over the first 60 minutes.
Add potassium chloride to fluids according to serum potassium: none above 5.5 mmol/L, 40 mmol/L when 3.5 to 5.5 mmol/L, and obtain urgent senior review below 3.5 mmol/L.
actions.timeframe: With each fluid bag after potassium review

actions.instruction: Start 10% glucose at 125 mL/hour when blood glucose falls below 14 mmol/L while continuing insulin for ketone clearance; consider reducing the insulin rate to 0.05 units/kg/hour.
actions.timeframe: When blood glucose is below 14 mmol/L

actions.instruction: Avoid a priming insulin bolus and do not routinely use bicarbonate or phosphate.

medicines.indication: Fixed-rate intravenous insulin infusion for adult diabetic ketoacidosis
medicines.group: Adults meeting biochemical DKA criteria; use specialist adjustment for pregnancy, renal failure, heart failure, older age and young adults
medicines.dose: 0.1 units/kg/hour, prepared as 50 units soluble human insulin in 50 mL 0.9% sodium chloride
medicines.duration: Continue until ketones are below 0.6 mmol/L and venous pH is above 7.3, with clinical review and safe transition to subcutaneous insulin
adjustments: Continue the person's long-acting basal insulin at the usual dose and time.
When glucose falls below 14 mmol/L, start 10% glucose and consider reducing the fixed-rate infusion to 0.05 units/kg/hour.
Escalate if ketones are not falling by at least 0.5 mmol/L/hour or bicarbonate is not rising by at least 3 mmol/L/hour.
monitoring: Venous pH, bicarbonate and potassium at 60 minutes, 2 hours and every 2 hours thereafter.
Laboratory electrolytes at least every 4 hours and continuous clinical assessment of fluid balance.
